story_type: ocean rowing race crew hurt far offshore, swimmer climbs aboard the rowboat, both rowers hoisted
hook: Two women rowing across the Pacific. One got hurt 150 miles out.
narration: Two women were rowing a tiny boat across the Pacific. Then one of them got hurt.
They were in the Great Pacific Race, a hundred and fifty miles west of Point Conception, California.
She had injured her wrist, so a Coast Guard Jayhawk flew out from San Diego.
A rescue swimmer rode the cable down into the open ocean.
He swam to the rowboat and climbed aboard beside them.
A hoist works best away from a small boat, where the cable can't snag on its rails and antennas.
[short pause] The basket came up first with the injured rower.
Then it went back down for her teammate.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew airlifted the injured rower and her teammate off the Pacific.
